The final-state covariance between flow and mean transverse momentum fluctuations, with its normalized correlation, is the most promising measurable probe. The radius-matched $^{48}$Ca follows $^{48}$Ti closely, and the position of $^{48}$Ti relative to the skin configurations depends on its radius. These collisions, analyzed with second-moment and shape-size correlators, offer a promising independent constraint on the $^{48}$Ca neutron skin at the LHC.

papers.title: Hot and dense QCD equation of state from the complex Langevin equation
papers.abstract: We discuss the QCD equation of state at temperatures above the crossover and for high baryon chemical potentials, obtained via the first ever complex Langevin simulations at the physical pion mass. In particular, we present continuum-extrapolated results for the energy, entropy, and enthalpy densities, as well as for the specific heat capacity as a function of baryon chemical potential and temperature.

papers.title: The Non-Relativistic Limit of Five-Dimensional Boson Stars and Scale Invariance Violation
papers.abstract: We investigate the non-relativistic limit of spherically symmetric boson stars in (4+1)-dimensional general relativity (GR). In this limit, the resulting Newtonian theory exhibits an exact scale invariance, leading to a critical boson star configuration with a fixed global U(1) charge and vanishing binding energy. We identify the origin of these properties in the restored scale symmetry and analyze how relativistic and gravitational corrections break this symmetry. By comparing the full (4+1)-dimensional Einstein-Klein-Gordon system with the Wick-Cutkosky model, we quantify the effects of these corrections on the energy-charge relation and the kinematic stability of the configurations. Our results demonstrate how weak violation of scale invariance lifts the degeneracy of the non-relativistic solutions and determines the behavior of boson stars away from the critical limit.

papers.title: Conformal Spectrum of (Super) Chiral Ising and XY Models
papers.abstract: We determine the spectrum of scaling dimensions of composite operators in the critical Gross-Neveu-Yukawa and Nambu-Jona-Lasinio-Yukawa models through a next-to-leading order semiclassical computation. Their infrared fixed points belong to the chiral Ising and chiral XY universality classes, respectively. At next-to-leading order, we resolve the Lorentz structure of the operator spectrum. For the parameter values at which supersymmetry is expected to emerge in the infrared, we obtain a closed-form expression encoding the full spectrum within the semiclassical methodology. The resulting organization of operators into superconformal multiplets provides further evidence for emergent superconformal dynamics.

papers.title: Running cosmological constant in light of recent CMB-BAO data
papers.abstract: We revisit single-field slow-roll inflation driven by a running cosmological constant, i.e. a cosmological constant receiving a logarithmic radiative correction, in light of the latest CMB-BAO data. The relative radiative correction $δ$ is treated as a free parameter of the model and allowed to be positive or negative. For positive $δ$, the predictions interpolate between a logarithmic regime and a linear inflation one. Compatibility with CMB-only data is confined to a narrow stripe near the $2σ$ border where $δ$ is relatively large. On the other hand, the predictions fit easily within the constraints including BAO data in a wide range of parameters. For negative $δ$, the slow-roll approximation breaks down at small field values and the predictions are excluded by data. However, once the effective mass contribution inside the logarithmic correction is taken into account, the negative $δ$ potential develops a local maximum and behaves like a hilltop model, achieving compatibility with CMB-only data, while agreement with CMB-BAO data is possible only at $2σ$.

papers.title: Certified Access: Test-Time Compute on Conservative Physics-Structured AI Memory
papers.abstract: Test-time compute mechanisms, such as retries, confidence-based escalation and non-local routing, are conventionally deployed as black-box additions to trained models. They typically add forward passes or halting heads, but give no structural account of what the extra compute buys or what it costs against the model's stability guarantees. We therefore propose a theoretical and empirical framework for test-time compute on a Latent Dynamics Model used as the memory. When an encoder's latent state $(q,p)$ is advanced by a damped symplectic (velocity-Verlet) step of a learned Hamiltonian, every mechanism that expands access has an exact phase-volume Jacobian, a bounded energy change and an exact latch-transport law. We split reachability failures into escape failures and reach failures. A Lorentz squeeze resolves escape failures by injecting bounded, re-absorbable energy. A gated canonical translation (a one-step channel across $C_T$) resolves reach failures at $\detJ=1$ exactly. We verify this certificate stack on a designed analytic testbed. Reaching just beyond $C_T$ with the squeeze requires energy that grows quadratically in the excess distance. The gated channel's energy cost equals the potential difference between its endpoints, which is zero on the matched channel measured here, and so does not grow with distance in this testbed. An untrained state-replacing map annihilates phase volume and erases stored charge, while the gated channel transports it. On a learned physics-structured memory, we show calibrated compute rationing and evaluate the scaling limits of non-local routing against a physics-free baseline. The main contribution is the formalization and verification of the certificate stack, not benchmark performance.

papers.title: Neutron Optical Constraints on Exotic Parity-odd Interactions between Neutrons and Nucleons
papers.abstract: Many theories beyond the standard model of particle physics predict the existence of weakly-coupled exotic spin-dependent interactions between standard model particles. We use experimental upper bounds on neutron-nucleus parity violation at meV and keV neutron energies in the forward scattering limit described by neutron optics to constrain exotic parity-odd interactions of the neutron with nucleons from exotic vector boson exchange for force ranges between $10^{-2}$ to $10^{-14}$ meters.

papers.title: Cosmological axion-photon interactions with a nonminimal dark gauge sector
papers.abstract: We study the cosmological evolution of radiation and dark radiation with nonminimal axion-photon-dark photon couplings. The Chern-Simons-type axion-gauge field interactions between the dark and visible sectors can induce energy conversion between photons and dark photons as well as polarization rotation during the propagation of radiation, leading to CMB spectral distortions and cosmic birefringence. Using the observed CMB monopole spectrum, we constrain the photon-dark photon energy conversion fraction, which is determined by the coupling constants and the evolution of the axion field. We further show that the parity-odd mixing interaction $φF\tilde{B}$ can partially relax the constraints on the standard axion-photon coupling, $φF\tilde{F}$, derived from the current observational limits of the cosmic birefringence angle.

papers.title: Cosmological constraints on extra radiation and early dark energy with lepton asymmetry and varying quark masses
papers.abstract: We investigate cosmological constraints on extra radiation and axionlike early dark energy (EDE), allowing primordial lepton asymmetry or light-quark-mass variation during big bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). We combine Planck CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+ supernovae, and primordial helium and deuterium measurements. When both extra radiation and lepton asymmetry are allowed, we obtain $N_{\rm eff}=3.27\pm0.16$, $ξ=0.017\pm0.011$, and $H_0=69.24\pm0.92\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$. A positive lepton asymmetry compensates the helium increase caused by extra radiation, allowing a higher inferred Hubble constant even with the LBT helium measurement, which agrees with standard BBN. For EDE, primordial-abundance measurements instead restrict the higher baryon densities associated with larger EDE fractions, which reduce the predicted deuterium abundance. Allowing lepton asymmetry does not relax this restriction. In contrast, a positive light-quark-mass variation increases deuterium and compensates this reduction, permitting larger EDE fractions and a higher inferred Hubble constant. The same variation leaves the extra-radiation constraint nearly unchanged. We also find that allowing lepton asymmetry relaxes the 95\% upper limit on the summed neutrino mass from $0.0640\,{\rm eV}$ to $0.0777\,{\rm eV}$ in the extra-radiation model.

papers.title: Dwarf Galaxy Reticulum II's MeerKAT L-Band Observation: Constraining WIMP Dark Matter
papers.abstract: The nature of dark matter remains one of the most profound open questions in modern physics, with weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) among the leading candidates proposed to account for the observed anomalies across cosmic scales. If WIMPs annihilate or decay in the dense dark matter haloes of nearby galaxies, the resulting high-energy electrons/positrons can produce synchrotron radiation in the presence of ambient magnetic fields, yielding a potentially detectable radio signature. Dwarf spheroidal galaxies are particularly promising targets for indirect dark matter searches due to their high mass-to-light ratios and low astrophysical foreground contamination. While radio observations have been widely used to constrain WIMP properties in these systems, the resulting limits remain highly sensitive to poorly constrained magnetic field assumptions. Here we utilize L-band ($1.3$--$1.5$ GHz) observations from the MeerKAT array directed towards dwarf galaxy Reticulum II and measure the surface brightness profile across the dwarf galaxy. Combining these measurements with theoretical models of WIMP annihilation and yield 95% confidence level upper limits on the WIMP annihilation cross-section $\langleσv\rangle \lesssim 10^{-26}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ for masses $m_χ\sim 10$-$200$ GeV (with the assumed uniform magnetic field model and diffusion constant). As next-generation radio facilities such as the Square Kilometre Array come online, robust characterisation of magnetic environments in dwarf galaxies will be essential to fully exploit their sensitivity to the particle nature of dark matter.

papers.title: HWF Analysis of TRN Black Holes
papers.abstract: We extend the horizon wave-function (HWF) formalism to a spherically symmetric, charged, spinless quantum source in $\mathcal{D} + 1$ dimensional spacetime geometry and construct the HWFs associated with inner- as well as outer-horizons of the Tangherlini--Reissner--Nordström (TRN) black hole. The corresponding black hole formation probabilities, $P_{\rm BH}^{\pm}$, are also calculated and their sensitivities due to various source parameters including charge, mass, and $\mathcal{D}$ are analysed as well. Our analysis reveals that the ratio of inner- to outer-horizon probabilities, $P_{\rm BH}^{-}/P_{\rm BH}^{+}$, changes drastically from being unity as the source departs away from being in the extremal limit defined by $α$ ($\to 1$ for extremal case). Furthermore, black hole formation probabilities are found to be highly suppressed for higher values of $\mathcal{D}$, particularly for the source mass, $m \lesssim Λ_{\mathcal{D}}$, e.g., for $α= 0.5$, the ratio, $P_{\rm BH}^{+}(\mathcal{D} = 5)/P_{\rm BH}^{+}(\mathcal{D}=10)$ turn out to be approximately $2.95\times10^3$, $117$, and $3.35$ respectively for $m/Λ_{\mathcal{D}} = 0.5, 1$ and $2$, with $Λ_{\mathcal{D}}$ being the reduced gravity scale associated with $\mathcal{D}$ spatial-dimensions.

papers.title: RAKI: High-Order Alternative Finite Differences for General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Binary neutron star (BNS) and black hole--neutron star mergers are among the most important multimessenger sources. Observations of these events could provide valuable insights into several unresolved phenomena, ranging from the efficiency of magnetic field amplification during and after mergers to the formation of magnetars and jets. Understanding these phenomena requires accurate modelling of magnetic field evolution, which remains a challenge for state-of-the-art general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) simulations. In this work, we present \texttt{RAKI} (Relativistic Astrophysics Code Implementation of the Alternative Finite Difference Approach for GRMHD), the first GRMHD code to simulate BNS mergers using high-order alternative finite-difference methods with adaptive-order WENO (AFD-WENO-AO) reconstruction and a fully non-staggered, node-centred vector-potential formulation. The code achieves up to ninth-order convergence in smooth test problems while accurately capturing discontinuities. In magnetised Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff (TOV) star tests, \texttt{RAKI} retains $99.2$ per cent of the initial maximum magnetic field strength over ${\sim}2$ ms, exhibiting an order of magnitude less magnetic field loss than a reference GRMHD code at the same resolution. In BNS merger simulations, fifth-order AFD-WENO-AO reconstruction yields approximately third-order convergence of the gravitational-wave phase in both magnetised and unmagnetised models. The discrete no-monopole constraint is preserved to machine precision without staggered grids, even during BNS mergers with moving refinement regions. These results establish \texttt{RAKI} as a high-order, non-staggered GRMHD framework for accurate modelling of magnetic field evolution in neutron star mergers and its implications for multimessenger astrophysics.

papers.title: Looking for gravitational waves with orbital dynamics: GUEST mission and the $μ$Hz band of Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: `Adding colour'' to the gravitational-wave sky by probing unexplored frequency bands has the potential to unveil new and unexpected phenomena in the Universe. The microhertz band, between pulsar timing arrays and LISA, is a particularly attractive target: it should host the extension of the signal recently found by pulsar timing arrays (if it is generated by a family of sources of gravitational waves), and it may harbour signals from the early Universe, primordial black holes or dark matter. In these proceedings, we review how the orbits of gravitationally bound systems act as resonant detectors of microhertz gravitational waves and ultra-light dark matter. We then describe GUEST (Gravitational Universe Exploration with Satellite Tracking), a mission concept recently proposed to the ESA F-class call, consisting of two dense passive spheres covered with retroreflectors, placed in highly eccentric Earth orbits and tracked by a global laser-ranging network.

papers.title: Enhanced Signal and Excited-State Control in Nonlocal Lattice Correlators
papers.abstract: Nonlocal correlation functions underpin lattice calculations of parton physics. However, their extraction is limited by a rapidly deteriorating signal-to-noise ratio with increasing Euclidean separation and hadron momentum, and by excited-state contamination. We propose a new fitting strategy that enhances control over both: by taking the ratio of nonlocal to local correlators, we can project out the dominant ground-state dynamics with a signal that is much cleaner and far less sensitive to excited states than the conventional approach. We demonstrate the method on the quark and gluon PDF, the quark GPD and TMDPDF. The results are consistent with those from the conventional three-point/two-point ratio fit but exhibit markedly improved precision and stability, and extend the accessible range to larger hadron momenta. For nonforward matrix elements such as GPDs, our strategy greatly simplifies the analysis procedure. Our method applies to general Dirac and momentum structures, for connected and disconnected contributions, and extends naturally to other nonlocal correlators, making it immediately deployable in existing lattice programs toward precision hadron structure.

papers.title: Phenomenological implications of cosmic (super)strings with time-varying tension
papers.abstract: Cosmic strings and cosmic superstrings could have formed in the early universe. In a particular class of models, the tension associated with these defects is time dependent, either because the strings themselves are composed of evolving moduli fields, or because they are directly coupled to evolving scalar fields leading to an effective time dependence in the string tension. Here we take seriously the possibility of this time dependence and investigate the phenomenological consequences of such an evolution, comparing the results to the more traditional case of a fixed time independent tension. In particular, for five different time varying models, motivated by different possible forms of evolution of the string tension, we evaluate their Gravitational Wave (GW) contributions as well as their impact on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). Performing an MCMC analysis of the models we find there are indeed interesting spectral signatures in the GW emission at frequencies between the current PTA and interferometer data, but the signatures are not unique to these strings, making them hard to pin down using current data. However, we do find cosmic strings with evolving tension fit the GW data as well as other favoured models.

papers.title: At the EDGES of MADness: phenomenology of relic millicharged atomic dark matter
papers.abstract: Millicharged dark matter lives in a corner of parameter space that has been considerably shrinking over the past decades, due to constraints from cosmology, astrophysical systems, and ground-based experiments. A particularly interesting probe is the 21-cm absorption signal at Cosmic Dawn, which attracted interest in light of the EDGES claim: the reported excess absorption can be explained by millicharged dark matter with a fractional electric charge of~$10^{-6} \lesssim ε\lesssim 10^{-4}$, but it must be a subpercent of the total dark matter abundance to remain consistent with the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We show that very low fractions of millicharged dark matter naturally arise from atomic dark matter: a dark sector model that replicates the physics of standard atomic hydrogen. Dark ions undergo the process of dark recombination, leaving a relic ionized component that, in the presence of kinetic mixing, is naturally millicharged. We modify the cosmological Boltzmann solver CLASS to incorporate this scenario, and we investigate the parameter space of millicharged atomic dark matter (MAD) that is allowed by CMB, large-scale structure, and supernovae data. We find there are cosmologically viable regions of MAD parameter space that are consistent with laboratory and astrophysical bounds and also overlap with the EDGES-defined window. Although the EDGES result is likely not a Cosmic Dawn signal, MAD leaves distinctive cosmological signatures, accessible to upcoming 21-cm observations.

papers.title: Comments on $\bf{η'}$ nuclei and on the $Λ$ binding energy of the hypertriton
papers.abstract: I briefly discuss two apparent puzzles: (i) is the observation of $η'$(958) bound states in $^{11}$C at GSI [1] compatible with a nearly vanishing real part of $η'N$ scattering length [2]? and (ii) is the $Λ$ binding energy of the hypertriton (${{_Λ}^3}$H), the lightest particle-stable hypernucleus, very small (63$^{+38}_{-31}$ keV, J-PARC E73 [3]) or very large (523$\pm$76 keV, MAMI [4])? Here, I suggest that MAMI's observed weak-decay pion momentum peak originates from ${{_Λ}^7}$He, not from ${{_Λ}^3}$H \cite{Gal26}.

papers.title: Weak (quasi-)PDFs from the lattice
papers.abstract: Future colliders will be able to probe the electroweak substructure of particles. An accurate description of this substructure may necessitate electroweak PDFs, similarly to QCD. We investigate therefore the Higgs and W/Z PDFs in a reduced Standard Model setup using lattice methods, determining the quasi-PDFs, and, to lowest order, the resulting PDFs. While uncertainties remain, the results show interesting structures in line with expectations from gauge invariance.

papers.title: Complex potential and the thermal width of quarkonium in quark-gluon plasma
papers.abstract: We study the complex heavy quark anti-quark potential in lattice 2+1 flavor QCD at non-zero temperature. We point out a close relation between the imaginary part of the potential and the thermal quarkonium width. Using this relation, we estimate the thermal width of charmonia and bottomonia at high temperatures, which are not yet accessible with direct lattice QCD calculations of the quarkonium correlation functions and compare these to the results of the T-matrix analysis. For some of the excited quarkonia states, our estimates of the thermal width are smaller than the ones obtained in the T-matrix analysis.

papers.title: Going off the (momentum) grid: A simple implementation of noncold relics in linear Boltzmann solvers
papers.abstract: Linear Boltzmann solvers typically evolve the perturbations of noncold relics, such as massive neutrinos or hot subcomponents of the dark matter, on a momentum grid, often switching to a fluid approximation on small scales for efficiency. We implement in CLASS the Dispersive Fluid Approximation (DFA), a fluid scheme that captures the scale-dependent sound speed of these species. Within the standard ncdm module, the DFA significantly outperforms the default CLASS fluid approximation in the cross and neutrino power spectra, and reduces errors in the cold dark matter power spectrum by up to an order of magnitude, while adding only 1-4% to the total runtime. We also present the first open-source implementation of the Generalized Boltzmann Hierarchy (GBH), which simplifies the implementation of noncold relics by integrating out the momentum dependence of their perturbations altogether. Combined with the DFA and tested on massive neutrinos, the GBH reproduces the matter power spectrum to better than permille accuracy and cosmological parameter constraints to better than 0.05 sigma, at a computational cost comparable to that of the standard implementation. We argue that the GBH is particularly well suited to non-thermal relics whose distribution function varies with time or across parameter space. Our implementation of both the DFA and the GBH in CLASS is publicly available at https://github.com/aradn97/class_GBH.

papers.title: First search for sidereal and annual modulation of $Z$-pole asymmetries with the recovered SLD data set
papers.abstract: We report what is, to our knowledge, the first time-resolved analysis of electroweak asymmetries at the $Z$ pole, using the public release of the recovered SLD collision data: $6.6\times10^5$ polarized $e^+e^-\to Z$ events from the 1996-1998 SLC runs, with 385583 selected hadronic $Z$ decays spanning 782 sidereal cycles. The left-right asymmetry $A_{LR}$, reconstructed with the published SLD selection and per-event signed Compton polarization, shows no sidereal, solar-diurnal, or annual modulation; a simultaneous unbinned likelihood fit bounds the sidereal first-harmonic amplitude at 0.0086 (95% C.L., statistical). The analysis, frozen on the initial partial release, applied unchanged to the 229833 events of the later-released 1998 run confirms the null (amplitude 0.0018, p=0.90). Using the as-built SLC beam azimuth from the release's documentation corpus, we bound the asymmetry's anisotropy tensor in the Sun-centered frame: $ρ_1\le0.060$, $ρ_2\le0.18$, and, for vector backgrounds, $ρ_0\le0.092$ (95% C.L.). A leading-order matching maps these onto minimal Standard-Model-Extension coefficients as $10^{-2}$-level sensitivities to the two-time-index block of the electroweak gauge-sector coefficient $k_W$ (components with no existing laboratory constraint) and to the Higgs-sector coefficient $k_{φφ}$; the insertions split the $Z$ pole by polarization, so for the tensor families assessed the resonance saturates the sidereal amplitude near $10^{-2}$ and the Born-model bounds exclude finite coefficient bands rather than set an upper limit. We also derive a previously unpublished $Z$-pole birefringence channel in the helicity-odd azimuthal modulation of the thrust axis, with response enhanced by about $2M_Z/Γ_Z$; a Born-level pilot is null. First sidereal analyses of hadronization and leptonic asymmetries bound instrumental drifts at the $10^{-4}$-$10^{-3}$ fractional level.

papers.title: Quasinormal-mode encounters: Pseudospectra near Kerr--Newman exceptional points
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs), at which two quasinormal frequencies and their eigenvectors coalesce, can strongly enhance the spectral instability of black hole quasinormal modes. We investigate this behavior in Kerr--Newman spacetimes through pseudospectra and condition numbers for neutral massless scalar fields and coupled gravitoelectromagnetic (GE) perturbations. For the scalar field, we follow the $(\ell,m)=(1,1)$ spheroidal branch and derive the energy norm from the stress-energy tensor. For GE perturbations, we use a coupled four-field system equipped with a positive radiative energy. At the selected near-EP backgrounds, the condition numbers of both modes in the close pair exceed those of the two more-damped modes shown for comparison at the same background. Along a matched GE parameter path, the frequency splitting follows a square-root law and the condition numbers grow as the inverse square root of the distance to the EP. The pseudospectral contours resolve the transition from individual-mode sensitivity to the collective response of the pair. Within the discretized problems and energy norms considered here, these results quantify the amplification of spectral instability near EPs and provide a basis for studying their contribution to black-hole ringdown.

papers.title: Cosmological tests of chameleon dark energy with dark sector coupling
papers.abstract: Recent DESI measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations favor a value of $Ω_{\mathrm m}$ different from that preferred by Planck cosmic microwave background observations. Combined with supernova data, these observations suggest an evolving dark energy equation of state that crosses $w=-1$. As a potential solution to multiple cosmological problems, chameleon dark energy has attracted increasing attention in recent years. In this work, we constrain a chameleon model in which late-time cosmic acceleration is driven by a canonical scalar field nonminimally coupled to dark matter. At early times, the scalar field evolves under the combined influence of its potential and the nonminimal coupling, and its effective mass greatly exceeds the Hubble parameter. The chameleon model with energy transfer from dark energy to dark matter yields a best-fit improvement of $Δχ^2=-7.25$ relative to $Λ\mathrm{CDM}$, comparable to that for energy transfer in the opposite direction. Joint sampling over both coupling directions favors a nonzero interaction at $3.3σ$. Although no phantom field is introduced, the modified dark matter evolution produces an effective dark energy equation of state that crosses $w=-1$ at $z\simeq0.5$.

papers.title: Influence of $Δ$ resonances in hyperonic neutron stars on gravitational-wave inspiral signatures
papers.abstract: The composition of dense matter in neutron star interiors remains uncertain, with the possible appearance of the non-strange $Δ$ resonances providing an important source of theoretical uncertainty. In this work, we investigate the gravitational wave signatures of hyperonic neutron stars containing $Δ$ baryons within a density-dependent relativistic mean-field framework based on the DDME2 parametrization. Within this framework, the baryons interact among themselves via mesons. For $Δ$ baryons, the interaction is uncertain to date. We investigate how variations of the scalar and vector $Δ-$meson couplings, subject to \(x_{σΔ}-x_{ωΔ}=0.2\), modify the tidal properties and inspiral gravitational-wave signals. We find that the allowed variation in the $Δ-σ$ coupling leads to substantial changes in the tidal properties of the neutron stars, which in turn leave distinct imprints on the gravitational-wave waveforms, particularly in their frequency evolution, accumulated phase, and strain amplitude. These waveform differences arise through changes in tidal deformability and are not unique signatures of $Δ$ resonances. Future gravitational-wave observations may therefore constrain the $Δ-$meson couplings within the adopted dense-matter framework, subject to degeneracies with alternative EOS models.

papers.title: FCC-μe: High Energy, High Luminosity Muon-Electron Collider & Neutrino Factory at CERN
papers.abstract: The concept is presented of making at the FCC-$ee$ (or CEPC) facility $μ^+e^-$ collisions at the centre-of-mass energy between 1 and 2 TeV and the average luminosity above $10^{34}$cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, concurrently to the $e^+e^-$ collisions. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including the exciting prospect of measurements of the Higgs boson self-interaction, and is followed by a presentation of the FCC-$μe$ layout -- from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations are also given regarding the machine-detector interface and the performance of the FCC-$μe$ and associated neutrino factory. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying relevance of such anti-muon beams for any future high energy storage ring as well as for neutrino science.

papers.title: Gravity between two masses beyond Newton's law
papers.abstract: Newton's law of universal gravitation describes the attraction between two masses through an inverse-distance potential. In Einstein's theory gravity gravitates: each mass reshapes the spacetime geometry through which the other acts. More than a century later, extracting the two-body interaction from this coupled geometry remains a fundamental analytical challenge. Even without motion or radiation, the static sector of the interaction harbours an infinite hierarchy of field couplings: the purest laboratory for gravitational non-linearity. Here we determine the static interaction from ninth to twelfth order in Newton's constant for arbitrary mass ratios, and derive a closed expression for the first backreaction beyond the Schwarzschild test-body limit to all orders in the gravitational coupling. We achieve both advances by formulating the problem around the stationary interaction energy. An exact one-body background resums one source's self-interaction, stationarity reduces the fields required from the other, and integrated response identities reveal cancellations across the coupled modes. Complementary expansions then resolve the complete mass dependence at finite order. Together, these results bridge the gap between an infinitesimal probe and comparable masses, exposing hidden analytical simplicity within Einstein's theory and providing essential building blocks for modelling orbital dynamics and gravitational-wave generation.

papers.title: On Geometric Observables in Gravity
papers.abstract: Measures of geometry like distance and time are staples of classical gravity. While geometric quantities arise broadly in quantum gravity, their graviton corrections are less explored. In this paper, we study geometric observables in perturbative quantum gravity. We form distance and time observables that model measurements, including in the presence of spacetime fluctuations. Gravitational dressing ensures these constructions are coordinate invariant. Then we show how these finite-distance observables become memory and Shapiro time delay operators upon taking asymptotic limits. We compute leading graviton effects in correlators of geometric observables throughout. Altogether, our results identify a class of geometric observables that link experiments and operations on the celestial sphere.

papers.title: Neutralino dark matter in gauge mediation
papers.abstract: We explore the potential of neutralino dark matter within the framework of gauge-mediated supersymmetry (SUSY) breaking. Gauge mediation offers an advantage over gravity mediation, as SUSY CP/flavor problems are avoided more easily, leading to significantly milder fine-tuning for electroweak symmetry-breaking compared to gravity mediation. In our models, the lightest neutralino, as the lightest SUSY particle (LSP), is a viable dark matter candidate, assuming a gravitino mass of $\mathcal{O}(100)~\mathrm{TeV}$. The models are formulated in five-dimensional space-time, where the SUSY breaking field and the matter fields are placed on separate branes to avoid issues related to flavor and CP violation, and the radion is stabilized by a supersymmetric Goldberger--Wise mechanism. Four distinct neutralino dark matter scenarios are studied: bino-wino coannihilation, higgsino dark matter, wino dark matter, and entropy-diluted bino dark matter. For each case, we determine the allowed parameter spaces and evaluate their consistency with existing experimental limits. Additionally, we examine the potential for testing these models through future investigations at the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) and through dark matter direct detection experiments.

papers.title: Models with rank-reducing discrete boundary conditions on $T^2/{\mathbb Z}_4$
papers.abstract: We study six-dimensional $SU(n)$ gauge models with rank-reducing discrete boundary conditions on the orbifold $T^2/{\mathbb Z}_4$, without and with continuous Wilson line phases. For the latter case, we find that a minimal model can describe the breakdown of the electroweak symmetry based on an $SU(6)$ gauge group. This model possesses excellent features that two Higgs doublets come from the zero modes of the extra-dimensional gauge field, and the quarks in each generation can be unified into one multiplet, without exotic quarks, as the zero modes of a bulk field in the $\boldsymbol{15}$ representation of $SU(6)$. There exists a vacuum where the electroweak symmetry is slightly broken by the Hosotani mechanism, with the addition of suitable bulk fields.

papers.title: Supernova cooling from neutrino-devouring dark matter
papers.abstract: Supernova cooling provides a powerful probe of physics beyond the Standard Model (SM), in particular for new, light states interacting feebly with SM particles. In this \textit{Letter}, we investigate for the first time the production of fermionic dark matter (DM) via the neutrino-devouring process inside a core-collapse supernova, which contributes to the excessive cooling of the supernova. By incorporating state-of-the-art supernova simulation data and the full time evolution information, we derive stringent and robust limits on DM interactions, which can improve upon direct detection limits by several orders of magnitude. We exclude the cross sections down to $10^{-51}-10^{-58}$~cm$^2$ in the keV-MeV mass range for DM-electron scattering, and $10^{-49}-10^{-56}$~cm$^2$ in the 0.1-100~MeV mass range for DM-nucleon scattering, supplemented by complementary constraints from cosmology, astrophysics, colliders and direct detection experiments in the larger cross section regime. We also close almost the entire window in which fermionic DM constitutes $\mathcal{O}(1)$ fraction of DM due to its coupling to electrons in the keV-MeV mass range.

papers.title: Dark Parton Shower Effects for Cosmic Ray Boosted Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We investigate the effects of dark parton showers on the direct detection of cosmic-ray boosted dark matter (CRDM), focusing on a dark-photon-mediated model with fermionic dark matter--electron interactions. Using a Monte Carlo framework to incorporate Sudakov form factors and kinematic dipole recoil schemes, we simulate the evolution of the CRDM energy spectrum under dark sector splitting. Our results reveal that dark parton showering induces an energy-dependent reshaping of the CRDM flux, particularly characterized by a depletion of the high-energy flux. For a dark matter (DM) mass of 1 keV and a coupling of $g_D=3$, the CRDM flux can be enhanced by up to a factor of 1.12 in the $\mathcal{O}(10^{-2} \sim 1)$ MeV energy range for $2m_χ\lesssim m_{A^\prime} \lesssim 10^{-2}$ MeV, whereas it is suppressed by more than 50% at energies around 100 MeV for $m_{A^\prime} \lesssim 10^{-3}$ MeV. We then translate these effects into experimental sensitivities for PandaX-4T, Super-Kamiokande, and JUNO. For $m_{A^\prime} = 10^{-3}$ MeV and $g_D=3$, the bounds on the kinetic mixing parameter $ε^2$ are relaxed by factors of 1.02, 1.6, and 1.4, respectively. Incorporating the effects of DM parton distribution functions (PDFs) at neutrino detectors alongside dark parton shower effects further relaxes these bounds.

papers.title: Melting LHC detectors: A novel search for stopped long-lived particles
papers.abstract: Particles at the TeV scale with lifetimes of a year or longer could have been abundantly produced at the LHC yet escaped detection because of backgrounds, and could still be trapped within detector materials. With gluinos in split supersymmetry as a working example, we show that these trapped particles can be recovered from detector materials once prepared in liquid form, for example, by melting silicon detectors, extracting liquid argon from the electromagnetic calorimeter, or constructing a large water pool near ATLAS or CMS. These liquid samples can then be processed using iterative centrifugation followed by mass spectrometry, enabling single-particle sensitivity in macroscopic samples. This method can potentially discover gluinos up to 3 TeV in mass at the HL-LHC. It can also improve upon existing limits for other long-lived particles. For example, it can discover the stop up to 2 TeV, and will also be sensitive to integer-charged particles in the TeV range.

papers.title: Next-to-Leading Order corrections to the Next-to-Eikonal DIS structure functions
papers.abstract: We compute next-to-leading order (NLO) corrections to next-to-eikonal (NEik) quark background contributions to DIS structure functions. Among NEik corrections, $t$-channel quark exchanges provide the lowest order contributions in $α_s$, and can be represented as insertions of the quark background field of the target. At NLO, we compute NEik corrections induced by both quark and gluon background fields, and suppressed by an explicit factor of $α_s$. We show that the NLO corrections to the NEik longitudinal structure function are finite, while those to the NEik transverse structure function exhibit rapidity and UV divergences. These divergences are analyzed, and the finite contributions are extracted.

papers.title: $Λ_b \to Λ$ Form Factors from Light-Cone Sum Rules with $Λ$-Baryon Distribution Amplitudes
papers.abstract: We compute the $Λ_b \to Λ$ transition form factors using light-cone sum rules based on $Λ$-baryon distribution amplitudes, including contributions up to twist--6. The analysis is performed for pseudoscalar, vector, and axial-vector $b\to s$ currents and for different choices of the $Λ_b$ interpolating current. We find that only the pseudoscalar interpolating current leads to numerically stable and phenomenologically viable form factors. The resulting form factors are parametrised using a $z$-expansion and applied to the rare decay $Λ_b \to Λ\ell^+ \ell^-$, yielding predictions for branching ratios in the low-$q^2$ region.

papers.title: Radiative generation of chiral vector operators in $b\to s ν\barν$ transition
papers.abstract: The recent Belle II evidence for $B^+ \to K^+ ν\barν$, combined with a suppressed branching fraction ratio $R \equiv Br(B^0 \to K^{*0} ν\barν) / Br(B^+ \to K^+ ν\barν)$, necessitates new physics contributing to both left- and right-handed vector operators. We perform a systematic topological classification of one-loop completions that radiatively generate both operators without tree-level mediation, and construct two minimal benchmark scenarios: a scalar-rich model and a fermion-rich model. Evaluating these frameworks under specific benchmark mass schemes and four distinct flavor structures, we find a generic anti-correlation where enhancing one decay channel typically suppresses the other. A notable exception is a decoupled flavor configuration within the scalar-rich model, which yields simultaneous constructive interference, reducing $R$ by $4.22\%$ while satisfying all complementary flavor bounds. Under a universal coupling assumption, the scalar-rich model yields exact cancellation in the charged mode, highlighting the non-trivial interplay between flavor structure and loop-generated Wilson coefficients.

papers.title: Investigation of the photoproduction of bottom-charmed baryons within NRQCD
papers.abstract: We present a further theoretical study of the orbital $P$-wave bottom-charmed baryon within the framework of nonrelativistic QCD, considering both the direct photoproduction channel $γ+γ\rightarrow Ξ_{bc} +\bar{c}+\bar{b}$ and the resolved photoproduction channel $γ+g \rightarrow Ξ_{bc} +\bar{c}+\bar{b}$. At future linear colliders, ILC and CLIC, the initial photons can be emitted from the laser backscattering and then the parton gluon can be emitted from the photon. The formation of $Ξ_{bc}$ can be modeled in two steps: a compact diquark state $\langle bc\rangle[n]$ is formed first and subsequently captures a light quark from the vacuum to hadronize into the baryon $Ξ_{bc}$. The color and spin quantum number $[n]$ of the $\langle bc\rangle$ diquark can be $[{}^3S_1]_{\bar{\textbf{3}}/\textbf{6}}$, $[{}^1S_0]_{\bar{\textbf{3}}/\textbf{6}}$, $[{}^1P_1]_{\bar{\textbf{3}}/\textbf{6}}$, or $[{}^3P_J]_{\bar{\textbf{3}}/\textbf{6}}$ with $J=0,1,2$. Using three benchmark collision energies and an illustrative integrated luminosity, we analyze the cross sections, differential distributions, and the estimated produced events of the $Ξ_{bc}$ baryon. For the conservative $h_{\mathbf{6}}=0$ baseline, the combined $P$-wave contribution amounts to approximately 8\% of the combined $S$-wave rate at three considered collision energies and is therefore non-negligible.

papers.title: Deeply virtual meson production at HERA and at the EIC within the Color Glass Condensate EFT
papers.abstract: Continuing our previous study of Deeply Virtual Meson Production (DVMP) at twist-3 accuracy, we derive compact expressions for all helicity amplitudes. We perform a phenomenological analysis of the helicity-amplitude ratio $\mathcal{A}^{11}/\mathcal{A}^{00}$ and of the spin-density matrix element $r_{00}^{04}$ within the Color Glass Condensate framework. Small-$x$ evolution is incorporated by numerically solving the running-coupling-and-collinearly-improved Balitsky-Kovchegov and Balitsky-Fadin-Kuraev-Lipatov equations with the McLerran-Venugopalan model as the initial condition. Our exploratory phenomenological study shows that parameters fitted to inclusive DIS data capture the shape of the measured helicity observables but overestimate their magnitude, indicating the need for a dedicated fit to exclusive data. To overcome its absence in the literature, we introduce an effective phenomenological matching prescription. Our results are then compared to HERA data, and predictions are presented for electron-lead collisions at the future Electron-Ion Collider. We discuss the impact of non-linear effects at low photon virtuality and the role of genuine higher-twist contributions associated with light vector meson distribution amplitudes, corresponding to higher-Fock-state components of the projectile.

papers.title: All-heavy tetraquarks with different flavors
papers.abstract: In a nonrelativistic potential quark model framework, we carry out a precise calculation of the mass spectrum of the all-heavy tetraquarks with different flavors, $bb\bar{b}\bar{c}$, $cc\bar{c}\bar{b}$, $bb\bar{c}\bar{c}$, and $bc\bar{b}\bar{c}$, by adopting the explicitly correlated Gaussian method. A complete mass spectrum for the $1S$ states is obtained. For the $bb\bar{b}\bar{c}$, $cc\bar{c}\bar{b}$, $bb\bar{c}\bar{c}$, and $bc\bar{b}\bar{c}$ systems, the $1S$ states are predicted to lie in the mass ranges of $ \sim(16.06,16.14)$, $\sim(9.65,9.74)$, $\sim(12.89,12.94)$, and $\sim(12.75,12.99)$~GeV, respectively. Moreover, by using the obtained masses and wave functions, we evaluate the fall-apart decay properties within a quark-exchange model. The results show that the $1S$ states of the all-heavy tetraquarks with different flavors may have narrow fall-apart decay widths, which range from a few tenths to several MeV. Some all-heavy tetraquarks with different flavors could be search for at LHC in their optimal fall-apart decay channels, such as $ΥJ/ψ$, $ΥB_c^-$, and $J/ψB_c^+$.

papers.title: LHC di-dijet excesses as signals of fourth-generation tetraquarks
papers.abstract: We postulate that the excesses of di-dijet events observed at the LHC are attributed to the production of four fourth-generation quarks $b'$ with a mass $m_{b'}\approx 2$ TeV at few-TeV scales. The di-dijet signals around the four-jet invariant mass $m_{4j}\approx 8$ TeV arise from a resonant $b'b'\bar b'\bar b'$ tetraquark production, where the dijet resonances of masses about 2 TeV correspond to $b'\bar b'$ first excited states (color-octet scalars with the principal quantum number $n=2$) in a Yukawa potential created by Higgs boson exchanges. Those around $m_{4j}\approx 3.6$ TeV originate from a non-resonant $b'b'\bar b'\bar b'$ production, where the dijet resonances of masses 0.95 TeV correspond to $b'\bar b'$ ground states (color-octet vectors with $n=1$). It is shown that a $b'\bar b'$ system with $m_{b'}\approx 2$ TeV in the Yukawa potential does generate the aforementioned bound state spectrum. We then illustrate that the observed excesses can be accommodated in our setup by translating the fourth-generation model to the effective theories containing color-octet scalars and vectors available in the literature. Simply speaking, our scenario can be viewed as a TeV-scale analogue of the search for a fully charmed tetraquark via the four-muon channels $X(6900)\to (c\bar c)(c\bar c)\to 4μ$ at a GeV scale.

papers.title: A dynamical implementation of colour coherence for quenched jets in JEWEL
papers.abstract: Colour coherence affects the radiation pattern of hard partons both in vacuum and in a dense coloured background formed in heavy ion collisions. In vacuum evolution it leads to the well-known phenomenon of angular ordering, and in heavy ion collisions the appearance of a medium resolution scale strongly affects the way in which a fragmenting hard parton interacts with the background medium. In this paper I present the implementation of colour coherence in the JEWEL event generator for jet evolution in a dense medium. In each interaction between a hard parton and the medium it is checked whether the momentum transfer of the scattering is sufficient to resolve the colour dipole. In this way it is dynamically decided which structures stay coherent. Importantly, scatterings that resolve an individual parton disrupt the colour coherence, which affects the next splitting via the loss of angular ordering. This leads to a suppression of hard radiation, and consequently a reduction in overall scattering rate, which is the dominant source of effects of colour coherence observable in reconstructed jets. I discuss these modifications using the examples of nuclear modification factor, jet fragmentation function and jet-hadron correlations.

papers.title: Revisiting predictions for cosmic-ray antinucleon fluxes from Galactic Dark Matter
papers.abstract: The data on cosmic antiprotons have reached an outstanding precision on energies spanning from GeV to hundreds of TeV, thanks to the space-based AMS-02 experiment. The balloon-borne GAPS experiment, which just completed its first Antarctic flight, will address antiproton and antideuteron fluxes well below GeV energies. Antinuclei in cosmic rays, as well as being produced by spallation reactions between cosmic-ray nuclei and the atoms of the interstellar medium, may hide contributions from exotic sources, such as particle dark matter annihilation in the Galaxy. In this paper, we present predictions for cosmic antiproton, antideuteron and antihelium fluxes both from secondary and dark matter origin. We use state-of-the-art production spectra, nuclear coalescence for antinuclei, and Galactic propagation models to derive upper limits on the dark matter annihilation cross-section from AMS-02 antiproton data in different propagation scenarios (BIG and QUAINT). We quantify the impact of future GAPS data, showing that its sensitivity to sub-GV antiprotons could improve the $\langleσv\rangle$ constraints by up to an order of magnitude for light DM ($m_χ \lesssim 50$ GeV). For heavier antinuclei, the detection perspective with existing and upcoming experiments are derived for those scenarios consistent with AMS-02 antiproton flux. The detectability of such signals strongly depends on the experiment, the propagation model, and the hadronization tuning. Our analysis underscores the complementarity of antinuclei channels for indirect DM searches and the critical role of low-energy windows in constraining light DM candidates.

papers.title: Lepton Flavor Violating Higgs decays at the Compact Linear Collider
papers.abstract: Lepton flavor violating Higgs decays could appear in scenarios beyond the Standard Model of particle physics. In this article, we study the sensitivity of a future Compact Linear Collider (CLIC) to such processes, namely, $h\rightarrow eμ$, $h\rightarrowτμ$, and $h\rightarrow eτ$. In the absence of any observation, 95\% CL\ upper limits in the region of $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-5}$ could be placed on the branching fractions of these processes, assuming integrated luminosities of $4$\,ab$^{-1}$ at $\sqrt{s}=1.4$ TeV and $5$\,ab$^{-1}$ at $\sqrt{s}=3$ TeV.

papers.title: Dark Matter Interpretation of the Super-Kamiokande Antineutrino Excess and Predictions for JUNO
papers.abstract: Super-Kamiokande has reported a small excess of electron antineutrino events in the 20 MeV energy range, in the search for the diffuse supernova neutrino background. We interpret this signal as a possible indication of dark matter that annihilates dominantly into neutrinos, pointing to a thermal dark matter candidate with $s$-wave annihilation and with mass in the tens of MeV range. This mass scale naturally fits into rich dark sector extensions of the Standard Model. Neutrino experiments, including JUNO, will be able to test this hypothesis in the coming years.

papers.title: A D_5 Model of Quarks with Explicit CP Violation
papers.abstract: The hierarchy of fermion masses and mixings lacks a self-consistent theoretical explanation at the dynamical or symmetry level, and the origin of CP violation remains unclear. These two issues have long been major challenges in particle physics. In this paper, we investigate the quark sector of a four-Higgs-doublet model with an exact D_5 symmetry. Within the framework of explicit CP violation, we consider the most general real vacuum, and perform a numerical fit of the quark mass spectrum and the CKM matrix using a Differential Evolution. We demonstrate that the model achieves an excellent overall goodness of fit with χ^2 = 6.97, and the Jarlskog invariant J_{CP} = 3.144 \times 10^{-5} agrees with the experimental value within 0.19σ. This indicates that the new source of CP violation provided by the model is consistent to generate the observed CP violation in the quark sector. Moreover, the hierarchies inherent in the vacuum expectation values and the quark Yukawa couplings naturally explain the observed hierarchy of the quark masses and mixing parameters.

papers.title: On Compositeness of $D_{s0}^*(2317)$ and its decay to $D_sπ^0$
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ can be described as a bound-state pole arising from the coupling between a discrete $c\bar{s}(1^3P_0)$ state and the $DK$ continuum state in the Lee-Friedrichs model. The elementariness and compositeness of the $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ are determined to be about $Z:X\approx 51.1 \%:48.9\%$, indicating a nearly equal admixture of compact quark-model state and hadronic molecular components. The decay width of $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)\rightarrow D_s^{+}π^0$ is evaluated within the quark rearrangement framework. The transition $c\bar{s}(1^3P_0)\rightarrow D_sπ^0$ proceeds via the OZI-allowed $c\bar{s}(1^3P_0)-D_sη$ coupling followed by $η-π^0$ mixing, which serves as the primary source of isospin violation in this channel. The coupling between $DK$ and $D_sπ^0$ is computed in a quark rearrangement model, where the isospin violation effect originates from the mass difference between the $D^0K^+$ and $D^+K^0$ thresholds. The parameters of the scheme shares the same ones with those of the underlying potential model and only the vacuum production strength is adjusted to reproduce the physical $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ mass. This calculation may shed more insight to the nature of exotic $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ state and its isospin-breaking decay properties.

papers.title: LIGO, LISA and Ultralight Axion-like Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Interferometric searches for axion-like dark matter (ALP DM) via the induced photon birefringence in a coherent background have been proposed and analyzed by several authors over the past decade, with tabletop experiments (LIDA, ADBC, DANCE) reporting first results and detailed calculations available for both ground-based (LIGO, GEO600 via DarkGEO) and space-based (LISA, TianQin, Taiji, BBO via Gué et al. and Yao et al.) gravitational-wave detectors. We revisit this class of measurements within the framework of Krauss (2019), and provide a detailed treatment of the interplay between the DM coherence length $λ_{\rm coh}$, the interferometer arm length $L$, and the detector transfer function, with attention to the distinct suppression regimes $λ_{\rm coh} > L$ (cancellation) and $λ_{\rm coh} < L$ (random walk). For LIGO the sensitivity is set by the Fabry-Pérot arm cavity response peaking sharply near the cavity free spectral range, reproducing the results of Nagano et al.; the naive single-pass estimate substantially overstates the reach and cannot be applied directly. For LISA, with the polarization-sensitive modification proposed by Gué et al. or Yao et al., the natural mass range $m_a \sim 4\times10^{-19}$--$4\times10^{-16}$ eV (LISA science band) is accessible and the projected reach $g_{aγγ}\lesssim {\rm few}\times 10^{-13}$ GeV$^{-1}$ (realistic optical-metrology noise) improves on the CAST bound over most of the band by up to about two orders of magnitude. We discuss directional signatures from the Galactic DM wind, both annual and sidereal, as a discrimination tool for candidate signals. Local DM substructure with anisotropic velocity dispersion can shift and enhance the reach in specific mass windows.

papers.title: New Energy-Loss Constraints on Dark Sectors from Deeply Inelastic Scattering with Initial State Radiation
papers.abstract: We employ the joint QED and QCD factorization of deeply inelastic, electron-proton scattering with generic initial state radiation to probe the possibility of exotic particle emission -- i.e., of weakly coupled particles originating from a dark or hidden sector -- through anomalous energy loss. We leverage this possibility through the consideration of phase-space-limited kinematic regions, for which the emission of an additional, undetected particle can particularly impact the associated cross-section. In this first paper, as a proof of principle, we focus on radiation from the incoming electron, considering the modification of the lepton distribution function from the emission of particles, that could have spin of up to 2 and various, well-motivated electron couplings. We illustrate the sensitivity of our approach through the computation of the modified cross-sections for the emission of MeV-GeV mass-scale, spin 0 particles in kinematics chosen for their sensitivity to initial state electron radiation and suitable to the forward-backward detection sensitivity of the ePIC detector at the EIC.

papers.title: Identifying $Σ(1380)$ and $Σ(1430)$ in the $J/ψ\to Λπ\barΣ$ reaction
papers.abstract: We study the $J/ψ\to Λπ\barΣ$ reaction by looking at the $π^+ Λ$ mass distribution at low energies, in search of signals for the low lying $Σ^+$ excited states. Apart from a clear signal of the $Σ(1385) (3/2^+)$ state, we find a smaller peak for the predicted $Σ(1430) (1/2^-)$, which has already been confirmed by the Belle Collaboration. A first analysis, considering only the $πΛ$ interaction, shows that the low energy part of the spectrum is better reproduced including contributions from the $Σ(1430)$ and the predicted $Σ(1380)(1/2^-)$ state that has been claimed before from analyses of different experiments. However, when we consider the $π\barΣ$ interaction the need for the $Σ(1380)$ disappears.

papers.title: Insight on confinement from the QCD effective charge
papers.abstract: Like the Gell-Mann--Low coupling $α$ of QED, the effective charge $α_{g_1}$ is a physical, observable-defined running coupling that can serve as the QCD coupling $α_s$. It can be represented by an analytic form consistent with renormalization-group evolution, holographic light-front QCD (HLFQCD), and the world data on $α_s$. As an observable, $α_{g_1}$ has a physically relevant analytic structure that reflects the underlying partonic dynamics. It displays, in the long-distance regime, two imaginary conjugate singularities at $Q^2 = \pm iΛ_s^2$, with $Λ_s$ the QCD scale. To connect this structure to confinement, we combine known general relations between $α_{g_1}$ and the parton dressed propagators and vertices with a recent phenomenological representation of $α_{g_1}$ within HLFQCD. Since, unlike vertices, propagators characterize a field variation between separate locations, the two singularities are assigned to the propagators. This results in the parton propagators displaying a long-distance behavior $e^{-Λ_s |x|/\sqrt{2}} |x|^{-5/2 + d_a}$ where propagation is suppressed beyond distances of order $1/Λ_s$, as expected from confinement. This offers an intuitive interpretation of confinement as the suppression of QCD Green's functions at long distance.

papers.title: Gravitational form factors of the pion in light-front holographic QCD
papers.abstract: Understanding the internal structure of the pion-particularly the energy-momentum distributions of quarks and gluons and the internal mechanical properties encoded in its gravitational form factors-is a fundamental challenge in quantum chromodynamics (QCD). In this work, we study the gravitational form factors using light-front QCD (LFQCD), combined with the holographic QCD. Our main innovation is the introduction of an effective light-front wave function, with its five-dimensional component obtained from holographic QCD, which is then employed, within the light-front QCD framework, to calculate the pion's gravitational form factors $A(Q^2)$ and $D(Q^2)$ as well as its radius. Our computed pion gravitational form factors show agreement with lattice QCD results, providing nontrivial support for the viability of our phenomenological model.

papers.title: Flavorful Interactions of AGN Neutrinos with Dark Matter Spike
papers.abstract: IceCube-Gen2 is going to make the dream of precise flavor ratio measurement for high energy cosmic neutrinos a reality. Motivated by this prospect, we build a model for the interaction of neutrinos with the dark matter and study the impact of the neutrino interaction with the dark matter spike around active galactic nuclei on the neutrino flavor ratio measurement. We show that, under certain circumstances, the flavor measurement by IceCube-Gen2 may discriminate between this model and the standard expectation, $(ν_e^\oplus:ν_μ^\oplus:ν_τ^\oplus)\simeq (1/3:1/3:1/3)$, as well as the prediction for a damped muon source. We discuss how we can derive information about the spike as well as about the characteristics of the dark matter particles composing it by combining the flavor ratio measurements with the results of the terrestrial experiments determining the neutrino mass ordering and a potential deviation from the standard model predictions in the measurements of the tau decay modes.

papers.title: Holographic spectral functions of exotic spin-1 mesons
papers.abstract: We develop a general holographic framework for computing thermal spectral functions of exotic spin-1 mesons. A bulk Proca mass encodes the canonical ultraviolet dimension of the interpolating operator, allowing channels with different ultraviolet scaling to be treated within a unified membrane-flow formalism in the zero-spatial-momentum limit. We test this framework in a soft-wall model with a gluon-condensate background for the hybrid $π_1$ and tetraquark-like $Z_c$ channels. The results show that dissociation temperatures of both channels lie below the phase transition temperatures. Increasing the gluon-condensate parameter $c$ delays dissociation in both channels, but through different effects: both the vacuum-mass shift and thermal spectral deformation contribute in the $π_1$ channel, whereas the latter dominates in the $Z_c$ channel. Nevertheless, for the same environment, the $Z_c$ resonance dissociates at a lower temperature than the $π_1$ resonance.

papers.title: Electromagnetic form factors of singly charmed baryons $Σ_c$ and $Λ_c$ in a covariant quark-diquark model
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of the spacelike electromagnetic form factors of the ground-state singly charmed baryons, $Σ_c$ ($Σ_c^{++},Σ_c^+,Σ_c^0$) and $Λ_c^+$, within a covariant quark-diquark model. Based on this framework, we obtain their magnetic moments as well as electric charge and magnetic moment radii. Such observables are important to understand the internal structure and the inner dynamics of these heavy baryon states. Our theoretical calculations are in qualitative agreement with available lattice QCD results of $Σ_c^{++}$ and $Σ_c^0$ baryons. We also discuss the mechanism behind the dependence of the numerical results on the charm quark and light diquark. A key finding is that the electric form factors of the singly charmed baryons fall off much more slowly with momentum transfer $Q^2$ than that of the proton, indicating a more compact electric charge distribution, which is attributed to the heavy charm quark acting as a localized core. More importantly, we observe a striking difference in the magnetic structure: while the magnetic form factors of $Σ_c$ are dominated by the light axial-vector diquark, those of $Λ_c^+$ are unexpectedly governed by the charm quark due to the vanishing contribution of the scalar diquark. This highlights the decisive role of the light-diquark spin configuration in determining the magnetic properties. Finally, using an empirical asymptotic relation connecting the spacelike and timelike regions, we predict the total cross section for $e^+e^-\toΣ_c\barΣ_c$. Our findings can be tested at existing facilities including the BESIII, Belle II and LHCb, as well as the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility.

papers.title: Determination of the $η$-$η^{\prime}$ Mixing Angle from $F_{η^{(\prime)}γ}(Q^2)$ within the Self-consistent Light-front Quark Model
papers.abstract: We study the $η$-$η^{\prime}$ system in the self-consistent light-front quark model (LFQM) with the quark flavor mixing scheme, where the single mixing angle is constrained by the transition form factors (TFFs) $F_{η^{(\prime)}γ}(Q^2)$. A continuous combined $χ^2$ fit to the CLEO and BABAR data gives $θ=41.55^{+0.57}_{-0.60}\,{}^\circ$, in close agreement with the recent LHCb result $(41.6^{+1.0}_{-1.2})^\circ$. Using this mixing angle, we calculate the decay constants, light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs), Gegenbauer moments, $ξ$-moments, transverse momentum moments, electromagnetic interaction radii and two-photon decay widths of the $η$ and $η^{\prime}$ mesons. The predicted $a_2^η$ and $\langleξ^2\rangle_η$ are consistent with the latest BABAR results, and the electromagnetic interaction radii also agree well with the A2 and BESIII measurements. These results demonstrate that TFF data strongly constrain the light-front description of the nonperturbative properties of the $η$-$η^{\prime}$ system. After the fit and LFQM-input uncertainties are propagated, the predicted widths are $0.428^{+0.038}_{-0.035}$ keV and $3.067^{+0.190}_{-0.180}$ keV for $η\toγγ$ and $η^{\prime}\toγγ$, respectively. The central values are lower than the corresponding experimental values, indicating that the real-photon point provides a more sensitive test of the absolute TFF normalization.

papers.title: The QCD Axion and Neutrino Masses
papers.abstract: The strong CP problem and the origin of neutrino masses are among the clearest motivations for physics beyond the Standard Model. The Peccei-Quinn mechanism offers an elegant dynamical solution to the strong CP problem, predicting the QCD axion, while neutrino masses point to new degrees of freedom or interactions beyond the Standard Model. We explore the possibility that these two phenomena arise from a common origin by identifying the Peccei-Quinn symmetry-breaking scale with the scale responsible for neutrino mass generation. We perform a systematic and unified analysis of this connection in both DFSZ and KSVZ realizations of the Peccei-Quinn mechanism, considering the Type-I, Type-II, and Type-III seesaw mechanisms, the Zee radiative model, and the colored seesaw. For each scenario, we determine the axion couplings to photons and neutrinos and examine their phenomenological consequences. A robust prediction of all the frameworks considered is the existence of axion-neutrino couplings. We show that these interactions can significantly affect the axion decays. If the QCD axion makes up the observed dark matter, these couplings also lead to a large monochromatic neutrino flux from axion decays, opening a complementary path to test these theories in future neutrino experiments.

papers.title: Flavor-Violating Higgs and Top Decays in the Type 1B Flavorful Two-Higgs-Doublet Model with a Twist
papers.abstract: We study flavor-violating decays of the SM-like Higgs boson and rare top decays in the Type 1B realization of the flavorful two-Higgs-doublet model with a twist, focusing on $h\to sb$, $h\to db$, $h\to uc$, $h\toμτ$, $h\to eτ$, $h\to eμ$, $t\to ch$, and $t\to uh$. We present the relevant amplitude and branching-ratio formulae, include one-loop vertex corrections, and impose constraints from Higgs signal-strength measurements, electroweak precision tests, meson mixing, $B\to X_sγ$, direct HFV searches and CLFV constraints, including $μ-e$ conversion. The surviving parameter space favors $\mathrm{BR}(h\to sb)\gg\mathrm{BR}(h\to db)$, $\mathrm{BR}(t\to ch)\gg\mathrm{BR}(t\to uh)$, and $\mathrm{BR}(h\toμτ)\gg\mathrm{BR}(h\to eτ)\sim\mathrm{BR}(h\to eμ)$ in the lepton sector. One-loop effects usually preserve these hierarchies, but can modify individual channels through different mechanisms: sizable destructive tree--loop interference can reduce $h\to sb$ enough to yield rare $\mathrm{BR}_{\mathrm{1L}}(h\to db)>\mathrm{BR}_{\mathrm{1L}}(h\to sb)$ points, whereas the large relative corrections found in rare top decays mainly reflect strong SM-like alignment suppressing the tree-level amplitudes.

papers.title: Radiative decays of the predicted P-wave $D\bar{D}^*$ molecular state: The $0^{-+}$ case
papers.abstract: In the present work, we study the radiative decays of the $P$-wave $D\bar{D}^*$ molecular state $G_0$ with $I^G(J^{PC})=0^+(0^{-+})$ using a phenomenological Lagrangian approach. The molecular coupling is fixed by the compositeness condition with a Gaussian form factor. The partial widths for $G_0\to γγ$, $γJ/ψ$, $γψ(2S)$, $γh_c$, $γρ$, and $γω$ are evaluated. Our results show that the two-photon and $γh_c$ channels are highly suppressed, while $γJ/ψ$, $γψ(2S)$, and $γρ$ are of the order of a few keV, and $γω$ reaches several tens of keV, making it the dominant radiative mode. The ratios $Γ(G_0 \to γψ(2S))/Γ(G_0 \to γJ/ψ)$ and $Γ(G_0 \to γω)/Γ(G_0 \to γρ)$ are predicted to be $1-2.6$ and $3.4-5.4$, respectively, with mild parameter dependence. We also compare with hadronic decays and find that the total radiative decay width is lower than the hadronic decay widths by about one order of magnitude. We propose searching for $G_0$ in the sequential decay $Y(4230)\to γG_0 \to γωJ/ψ$, which is accessible to further experimental measurements by the BESIII, Belle II and LHCb Collaborations.

papers.title: Neutrino Direct Simulation Monte Carlo: Accurate modeling of out-of-equilibrium decaying cosmological relics
papers.abstract: We consider nonstandard cosmologies in which decaying relics inject energy at MeV temperatures, driving neutrinos out of equilibrium. The subsequent neutrino evolution shapes predictions for the cosmic radiation density and primordial light element abundances. Earlier work introduced Neutrino Direct Simulation Monte Carlo ($ν$DSMC), which describes neutrino transport through Monte Carlo sampling of particle interactions. Here, we extend this method by jointly evolving the relic population, neutrino spectra, electromagnetic plasma, and cosmic expansion, and coupling this evolution to Big Bang nucleosynthesis. The framework includes direct and inverse decays of the relic, neutrino flavor conversion, quantum statistics, and pion production by energetic neutrinos. To reveal the physical impact of these effects and independently test $ν$DSMC, we compare several approaches to neutrino evolution across a range of nonstandard cosmological scenarios. We find excellent agreement with independent solutions of quantum kinetic or quasi-classical Boltzmann equations. Compared with these calculations, $ν$DSMC includes a broader range of physical processes and is substantially faster for strongly nonthermal neutrino populations. This makes broad, robust parameter scans for nonstandard cosmologies practical. We show that when departures from thermal equilibrium are large, approximations that average over neutrino momenta can give qualitatively incorrect predictions, including the wrong sign of the change in the effective number of neutrino species and substantially incorrect primordial nuclear abundances. We conclude that the extended $ν$DSMC framework enables reliable cosmological tests of new physics by following neutrino thermalization and its observable consequences.

papers.title: Reassessing the Connection Between the Color Glass Condensate and TMD PDFs
papers.abstract: Paying particular attention to the different types of gluons, collinear, soft and Glauber, we argue that, in its standard formulation, the CGC does not contain the collinear sector required for a meaningful comparison with TMD factorization. The CGC Wilson lines usually identified as part of the proton matrix element should instead be interpreted as the equivalent of a soft factor. Restoring the missing collinear exchanges, we obtain a new definition of small-$x$ PDFs from an explicit calculation of the DIS cross section using CGC Feynman rules. The resulting expression can be cast in a form resembling TMD factorization without being equivalent to it. Finally, we discuss the evolution of these small-$x$ PDFs with respect to the rapidity cutoff $Λ$ and the Bjorken variable $x_b$.

papers.title: Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
papers.abstract: Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.

papers.title: Partial reconstruction of the decay $B_{s}^{0}\rightarrow φ(K^{+}K^{-})η' (π^{+}π^{-}η)$ at a future high-luminosity Z factory
papers.abstract: The decay $B_s^0 \to φ(K^+K^-)η'(π^+π^-η)$ is of particular interest in flavour physics because in the Standard Model it proceeds predominantly through the quark transition $\bar{b} \to \bar{s}s\bar{s}$. However, the reconstruction of this decay is experimentally challenging due to the presence of the neutral $η$ particle, which significantly reduces the overall reconstruction efficiency. In this study, the feasibility of using the partial reconstruction technique to reconstruct the invariant mass of the $B_s^0$ meson without explicitly detecting the $η$ particle is investigated. Monte Carlo simulated events corresponding to an FCC-ee environment are used, and the effects of detector momentum and vertex resolutions on the reconstruction performance are examined. The results show that improved vertex resolution substantially improves the global reconstructed mass response and partial-reconstruction efficiency, while improvements in momentum resolution are manifested primarily through a narrowing of the fitted central DCB component. These findings suggest that future high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders such as FCC-ee could effectively exploit the partial reconstruction technique to study rare decay modes containing undetected neutral particles.

papers.title: Information geometry of DGLAP evolution
papers.abstract: Quark and gluon splittings shift proton momentum toward smaller fractions with increasing resolution. Momentum conservation makes the summed momentum-weighted quark and gluon densities, when nonnegative, a probability distribution. We apply information geometry, the geometry of probability distributions, to this probabilistic form of Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi evolution. We evaluate, to our knowledge for the first time, the speed at which the shape of the proton's momentum distribution changes, measured by how well distributions at neighboring resolutions can be told apart statistically. We show that this speed has a closed-form lower bound at leading order, with one-loop splitting functions and running coupling, five fixed quark flavors, nonnegative quark and gluon densities and sufficiently regular inputs. Three numbers of the input (the distribution at the starting resolution) fix the bound at every scale without computing the evolved distribution, once the coupling is specified. The squared bound is at least 94.8 percent of the squared speed for three of the five model inputs at four scales from 2 GeV to 10 TeV. The bound is reached when the distribution's relative rate of change is linear in the logarithm of the inverse momentum fraction. The relative rate of change is close to this linear form in mean square weighted by momentum for these three model inputs at all four scales, and closer still to linear in the square root of the logarithm at the three higher scales. These descriptions are compatible because the logarithm and its square root are strongly correlated when weighted by these momentum distributions.

papers.title: Thermomagnetic enhancement of conserved-charge correlations in a lattice-constrained PNJL model
papers.abstract: Conserved-charge correlations offer a promising probe of magnetic fields in strongly interacting matter. We investigate their magnetic response and the finite-density equation of state within a lattice-constrained three-flavor Polyakov--Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model. A thermomagnetic scalar coupling, inferred by Gaussian process regression from lattice QCD results for the average light-quark condensate, incorporates inverse magnetic catalysis into the effective interaction. Without fitting conserved-charge observables, the resulting framework substantially improves their magnetic-field dependence and crossover behavior compared with the fixed-coupling model. In particular, it captures the pronounced magnetic enhancement of the baryon--electric-charge correlation and related susceptibility ratios, supporting their use as QCD magnetometers. The comparison demonstrates that the medium dependence of the effective interaction is essential to describe this response within the model. We further calculate pressure Taylor coefficients through sixth order and reconstruct the pressure and baryon density at nonzero baryon chemical potential. Our results show that lattice information from a single chiral observable constrains a broad thermodynamic response, connecting inverse magnetic catalysis, conserved-charge correlations, and the equation of state in a common framework. This provides a lattice-constrained basis for investigating magnetic-field signatures and finite-density thermodynamics in QCD matter.

papers.title: Soft factor of quasi-TMDPDFs from the soft limit of the quasi beam function
papers.abstract: The quasi-TMDPDF in large-momentum effective theory is related to the TMDPDF through a soft factor. We show how this factor arises from the quasi beam function itself. Computing the one-loop quasi beam function and decomposing it by the method of regions, we find that the hard and collinear regions give the matching coefficient and the lightcone beam function. The soft region involves only one lightlike direction, yet, once the two hemispheres of the gluon momentum are folded onto each other, it reproduces the square root of the lightcone soft function together with the reduced soft function. The analysis leads to an operator definition of the soft factor, as the vacuum matrix element of the soft Wilson lines into which the quasi beam function turns. This definition provides the basis for an all-order analysis, and it shows that the Collins-Soper kernel is reproduced to all orders.

papers.title: Reggeized $K^*(892)$ exchange in $π^- p \to K^0 Λ$ and implications for fixed-target measurements
papers.abstract: The two-body $π^- p \to K^0 Λ$ reaction provides a clean channel for studying strangeness production and producing tagged hyperon $Λ$ samples. We describe its total cross section over the $π^-$ beam momentum $2.6 \leq p_{π, {\rm lab}} \leq 6.0~{\rm GeV}/c$ using a single Reggeized $t$-channel $K^*(892)$ exchange without polarization. We also examine the implications for future fixed-target measurements. An idealized event sample is used to determine the laboratory momentum and polar-angle distributions of the charged particles from $K_S^0 \to π^+ π^-$ and $Λ\to p π^-$. The $K_S^0$ decayed two pions are strongly forward, whereas the proton and pion from the $Λ$ decay extend to larger angles and lower momenta. These distributions provide a kinematic baseline for future acceptance and tracking studies.

papers.title: Color-Reconnection Effects on the nMPI-Nch Conditional Multiplicity Fluctuations in PYTHIA 8 pp Collisions
